title: Conditional Endorsement: Simulating How Adults with Different Skills Evaluate Canada's National AI Strategy
abstract: arXiv:2611.19111v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Canada's 2026 national AI strategy, AI for All, commits to free AI training for everyone and to expanding business AI adoption, yet it is difficult to anticipate whether these policies will reach adults with uneven skills and circumstances. We ask how adults with diverse skills might rate these policies on support, effectiveness, and personal benefit, how their skills and circumstances shape these evaluations, and what implementation conditions they raise. We built 3,200 generative agents from a weighted sample of the Programme for the International Assessment of Adult Competencies (PIAAC) Cycle 2 respondents, collected their ratings and explanations for 20 policies, and analyzed dialogues between agents with contrasting ratings. The agents supported nearly every policy but were far less confident that they would improve adult AI literacy or benefit them personally. translated_title: 有条件的支持：模拟不同技能水平的成年人如何评价加拿大国家人工智能战略
translated_abstract: 加拿大2026年国家人工智能战略“AI for All（人人共享AI）”承诺为所有人提供免费的AI培训并扩大企业AI应用，然而这些政策能否惠及技能与处境不均衡的成年人仍难以预料。我们研究了具有多样化技能的成年人会如何从支持度、有效性和个人受益三个维度评价这些政策，其技能和处境如何塑造这些评价，以及他们提出了哪些实施条件。我们基于国际成人能力评估项目（PIAAC）第二轮受访者的加权样本构建了3,200个生成式智能体，收集了它们对20项政策的评价与解释，并分析了持有相反评价的智能体之间的对话。结果显示，这些智能体几乎支持所有政策，但对政策能否真正提升成人AI素养或使自身受益的信心要低得多。随着数字技术使用水平的下降，这一差距进一步扩大：基于……（注：摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究基于PIAAC数据构建3,200个生成式智能体，模拟不同技能水平的成年人对加拿大国家AI战略的评价，发现政策虽获普遍支持，但数字技术使用越少的群体对其有效性和个人受益的信心越低，呈现出“有条件的支持”态度。
en_tdlr: This study builds 3,200 generative agents from PIAAC data to simulate how adults with diverse skills evaluate Canada's national AI strategy, revealing broad but conditional endorsement—confidence in effectiveness and personal benefit drops sharply as digital technology use declines.
